slug: 2026-02-13 Namibia gets  Chinese satellite ground station

facts.fact: China handed Namibia its first satellite data receiving ground station at the Telecom Earth Station outside Windhoek, which will let Namibia receive satellite data for fields including agriculture, and the president asked all sector ministries and agencies to maximise its benefits.

systems.platform: ground station at Telecom Earth Station, Windhoek

facts.fact: Digital Earth Africa and SASSCAL agreed to build the AgriWatch dashboard on DE Africa Earth-observation products for crop-cycle, rangeland and rainfall monitoring, with AgriWatch covering this country among the six SASSCAL states.

The Namibian reports that a US$2.4 million government agreement with 6th Grain Corporation, since cancelled, was expected to use satellite imagery and geospatial analysis to monitor maize, millet, sorghum and wheat.

systems.owner: government of Namibia with 6th Grain Corporation

facts.fact: The agriculture ministry's agreement with 6th Grain Corporation was to use satellite imagery and AI to monitor staple crop production, and the firm says it submitted a report and half-built the farmer survey and registry software before Cabinet had the contract cancelled.
facts.system: Remote sensing agricultural agreement with 6th Grain

systems.system: Remote sensing agricultural agreement with 6th Grain
systems.owner: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Land Reform

facts.fact: A one-year Remote Sensing Agricultural Services Agreement worth US$2.4 million took effect on 16 June 2026 to build a national crop-monitoring system using satellite imagery to map agricultural land, monitor crop and pasture health and forecast staple crop production, before Cabinet ordered it cancelled.

systems.platform: satellite imagery, geospatial analysis and AI
systems.owner: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Land Reform

facts.fact: The Namibian reports a N$40 million contract awarded to 6th Grain in June 2026 to use satellite imagery and AI to monitor staple crops nationwide, which the agriculture ministry then terminated on Cabinet's instruction.

systems.system: Remote Sensing Agricultural Services Agreement (AI and satellite crop monitoring system)
systems.owner: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Land Reform

note: Only reports the cancellation of the AI and satellite crop-monitoring agreement, with no date for the award and no service stated.

facts.fact: The Windhoek Observer reports a one-year N$39.5 million agreement between the agriculture ministry and 6th Grain to use satellite imagery and remote sensing to monitor staple crops, improve crop forecasting and drought monitoring, with data owned by government.

systems.owner: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Land Reform

systems.system: Satellite ground data receiving station, Telecom Earth Station

note: Ground station for disaster, border and environmental monitoring; no farming use stated.

facts.fact: NASA Harvest says satellite-based tools and high-resolution cropland masks built for Namibia, provided to the Ministry of Agriculture, Water and Land Reform under a USAID-funded FAO pilot, were used operationally in 2023 and continue to support regular crop monitoring.
facts.system: NASA Harvest cropland masks and monitoring tools

systems.system: NASA Harvest cropland masks and monitoring tools
systems.owner: NASA Harvest and FAO with the Ministry

facts.fact: Minister Inge Zaamwani said the agriculture ministry had deployed the ERDAS APOLLO platform through the Office of the Surveyor-General as a central satellite imagery repository that will assist in monitoring crop health and assessing pastures.

note: Satellite work named is for SDG 6.6.1 water ecosystems, not farming.

facts.fact: FEWS NET's October 2026 Southern Africa seasonal monitor reports well-above-average NDVI vegetation in southern Namibia and below-average soil moisture in parts of the north and centre.

The Issue reports that the Ministry of Agriculture signed an agreement with US firm 6th Grain, worth US$2.4 million (about N$40 million), to deploy AI and satellite imagery crop monitoring across Namibia's staple crops; the government has opened a probe into the award.

systems.owner: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Land Reform
